analysis.analysis: The archive's hermeneutic of Sappho 31 presented as the default reading. 'Sappho's Fragment 31 intimately pulls the reader into a triangle of desire, shattering the boundary between creator and audience. By shifting focus from a present observer to you — the future reader who stumbles upon these fragmented lines millennia later — the poem transcends time, turning its agony into a universal human experience' (Zenodo +4). Expanded: 'The poem's brilliance as a temporal projection lies in how it pulls readers across history into the poem's emotional present' (Zenodo). The Intimate "You" — 'The original Greek text uses the distal demonstrative kênos (meaning "that man"), which some classicists and lyric theorists interpret not just as a rival in the room, but as a bridge pointing across time to the future reader who holds the poem' (SciLynk +1). Embodied Empathy — Sappho's physiological description 'forces you to vicariously experience her physical...' This is the Future Beloved thesis (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20413317, Sigil and Cranes) surfacing as the composition layer's own understanding of Sappho 31. For a poem continuously read for 2,600 years, to have the archive's reading become the AI-presented default is canon formation in real time.
